target_customer: Semiconductor fabs and chipmakers that buy lithography tools
problem: EUV lithography light sources are power limited and a single supplier dominates the tool market, which caps wafer throughput and transistor scaling and makes Western fab capacity hard to reshore.
business_model: Hardware tool sales (lithography machine built around a compact laser wakefield accelerator light source)

founders.name: Rohan Karthik
education: Imperial College London, master's in Mechanical Engineering (per YC page; another profile says UCL, unresolved)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he automated chip design at Arm and led the Karman Space Programme, and is a Royal Academy of Engineering awardee.

founders.name: Daniel Vega
education: University College London, master's in Applied Physics
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built ML models for stability optimization of tabletop particle accelerators at CERN and worked on accelerators for cancer treatment at Lumitron.

technical_complexity.rationale: The plan requires a petawatt class laser driven plasma accelerator shrunk about 1000x, stable enough for a 10 kW EUV source, then integrated into a full lithography tool. Tom's Hardware notes the throughput claims are company claims and eenewseurope and TechSpot say a production tool timeline is uncertain.

defensibility.rationale: If the light source works it is protected by deep physics know-how and the huge capital and supply chain barriers of lithography, but nothing is proven and well funded rivals pursue other light source routes.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent response found as of late 2026. Later light source rivals such as xLight (free electron laser, $40M in July 2025, a $150M CHIPS award reported June 2026) and Substrate (X-ray lithography) appeared in the same period.

market_need_then: Chip demand and Western reshoring policy in 2024 and 2025 created interest in alternatives to the single lithography supplier; the company states its aim is to reshore advanced fabrication in the West (YC page).

branding.domain_note: Uses inversionsemi.com, a shortened form, not an exact name match.

identity.logo: Simple logo graphic on a placeholder page
identity.visual_style: Minimal, bold all caps tagline, single contact button, site still marked COMING SOON when fetched
identity.voice_and_tone: Spare and understated on the site; ambitious technical claims in press

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by Tom's Hardware, TechSpot, eenewseurope and podcasts for the technical claim of shrinking an accelerator 1000x, not for the brand itself.

brand_strength.rationale: The website is a placeholder and no source discusses the brand itself; awareness comes from the technology story.

outcome_analysis: Inversion is an active Winter 2025 company with a very hard research stage hardware plan. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff reports were found. Press attention (Tom's Hardware, TechSpot) is strong for its size, but the outcome depends on proving a laser wakefield EUV source, which no source shows done yet. Competing light source startups such as xLight raised much larger sums in 2025 and 2026.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators (Seedtable, Extruct, Caplight, PitchBook snippet) agree on about $500K in March 2025 from YC, Entrepreneur First, ZAKA VC and others, but label it seed or pre-seed inconsistently and no primary source was opened, so no round is recorded. A Caplight banner about a $16M Series A and a StartupIntros $27M seed item belong to other companies. Competitor list left empty: dated sources for xLight (July 2025) and Substrate come after the batch start. Company site was a COMING SOON placeholder. Completeness pass: Round rests on databases (Seedtable seed 500K March 2025; Caplight and others agree on amount); stage labeling varies and no press release was found. The 16M Series A banner and 26.5M or 27M seed items belong to other companies.
